messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I've been trying to use the predict_snpgeno with the provided code:

probs <- calc_genoprob(magic, error_prob=0.002)
m <- maxmarg(probs, minprob=0.5)
inferg <- predict_snpgeno(magic, m)

And I'm getting this erro:
Error in ph[[chr]][, , 1] : incorrect number of dimensions

I checked the dimensions of my files and look alright:
> dim(m$`1`)
[1] 921 159
> dim(magic$geno$`1`)
[1] 921 159
> dim(magic$founder_geno$`1`)
[1]   8 159
> dim(magic$alleles)
NULL
> dim(probs$`1`)
[1] 921   8 159

Would you have any idea?

Thanks in advance!!

Jorge

Hi Karl,

Sorry to bother again as I'm immersing in the analyses of this pop we've been developing.

The allele frequency in some regions, especially in chr 11 (pic attached), has a weird pattern while one parent showing a frequency of zero or near zero and another parent showing a higher than expected frequency pattern in the same region. I was wondering if this some artifact of the calc_geno_freq or there really was some unintended selection against/for alleles in this region, but I doubt it.

I though about doing two things:
1)  Doing: reduce_markers (gmap, 1)
But I've been getting some error as:
Error in create_marker_index(lapply(cross$geno, colnames), map) : Some markers not found in map
I also tried to use pull_markers but haven't been able to get the reduced_marker into a list.

2) Eliminate those markers with parental allele frequencies above 0.20 or bellow 0.05.
I already took those out with less than minor allele frequency of 0.08 anyways.

Would you have any suggestion?

Sorry and thanks again.

Jorge

messages.body_plain:
It does happen that there can be selection for one particular founder in a region, and against some other founder.

I don't see how reduce_markers() would be useful in this case.
And the error that you're getting doesn't make much sense to me. Can you provide the full code that you're using?
If you want just the marker names from the output of reduce_markers(), you could do:

  reduced_map <- reduce_markers(gmap, 1)
  reduced_markers <- unlist( lapply(reduced_map, names) )

You could then use

  reduced_cross <- pull_markers(mycross, reduced_markers)

I wouldn't eliminate markers with high or low parental allele frequencies. If they reflect what's going on in the population, then you wouldn't want to eliminate them.

karl

messages.subject: Including a treatment effect
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would like to include a treatment in my model, but I am not sure how to do this. I am analyzing data from the DSPR RILs that includes individuals from 95 genotypes that were exposed to control conditions and individuals from these same genotypes that were exposed to stress conditions. I've tried including treatment as an additive covariate, but because each genotype is present twice in the phenotype dataset (I suspect), scan1 throws this error:

```
out <- scan1(dspr.pr <http://dspr.pr>, pheno_tcg[,1], TRT)
Error in get_common_ids(ind2keep, rownames(pheno)[rowSums(is.finite(pheno)) >  :
  Duplicate names in argument 2
```

Is there a more appropriate way to include my treatment effect, and by extension to build a more complex model that could, for example include an interaction between two treatment groups (i.e. response ~ treatment * tissue + resistance level, etc.)?

Cheers,
Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Including a treatment effect
messages.body_plain:
The individual labels need to be all distinct, so if you're going to double them, you need to add something to the IDs for one or the other or both. "_treated", "_control" or something like that.

But rather than doubling the lines and including a treatment covariate, I would be inclined to take the differences (treatment - control), or perhaps log(treatment/control) as a single phenotype for each RIL.

karl

The individual IDs within each of the genotype probabilities, phenotypes, covariates, and kinship matrix all need to be distinct and they need to match each other.

karl

messages.subject: Didn't converge error with binary model
messages.subject_clean: Didn't converge error with binary model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I'm get an error message running a binary scan in QTL2, and the output looks a little odd.
2: In scan_binary_onechr(genoprobs, pheno, addcovar, maxit, tol, qr_tol,  :
  binreg didn't converge
If I use the default model (obviously inappropriately, because it's a binary trait), I don't get quite such dramatic pits or the "didn't converge" error message (see below). Changing maxit doesn't seem to help.

For a little more context: this is a map from a non-model system (Rumex) with very unevenly distributed recombination (mostly at the tips of chromosomes). This is simply a scan to confirm the identity of the sex chromosome by localizing sex as a phenotype; multiple other sources of data (e.g. GWAS from a population, distribution of XY polymorphisms in a pedigree cross, etc.) localize the sex-linked region to the same part of the chromosome. There are almost certainly errors in our assembly (the genome is highly repetitive) and in our map (because there is very, very low recombination across most of the chromosome - about 3/4 of the physical map is actually localized at above 60cm).

Do you have any thoughts about what those dips are? I'm assuming they're picking up on errors in our assembly or map. And should we worry too much about the converging? This is mostly just another way to localize something we already know.

Thanks!

Joanna

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Didn't converge error with binary model
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl2-disc] Didn't converge error with binary model
messages.body_plain:
It's a warning not an error. The binary scan fits a logistic regression at each locus, which uses an iterative algorithm which is apparently not converging in the chosen number of iterations. You can also try playing with the arguments 'bintol' (the tolerance for convergence, default 1e-6) and 'eta_max' (maximum value of linear predictor, default ~28).

The dips in the LOD score likely correspond to positions where the algorithm is not converging.

karl
